title: Digitization, Prediction, and Market Efficiency: Evidence from Book Publishing Deals
eligible_reason: Single adoption date and no main data. The design compares romance vs other genres before and after 2008 (after = year > 2008, the e-book/self-publishing shock), so c.after#c.pmp_romance is a two-group single-date DiD on deal-level cross sections (areg with editor and other $fx absorbed FE, $control). Table 3 splits post into between/after3 (two post bins of the same single date). No unit-specific adoption dates. master_data.dta (Publishers Marketplace deal data) is proprietary and not shipped; README states only Figures 1a, 2a-b and 4 can be run with included data.
design_notes: Deal-level data on book publishing deals 2002-2016 (master_data.dta, 58,782 deals). Outcomes: absolute prediction residuals (abserr, abse), false positives/negatives, deal size. Treatment group: romance authors (pmp_romance = author ever has a romance deal). Post: deals after 2008. Figure 3/5: year x pmp_romance event-study around 2008 (reference 2008).
estimators_reported: two-group single-date DiD on repeated cross-sections (areg)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One shock year (after = year > 2008) applied to romance genre.

specs.exclusion_reason: single adoption date (2008) for one treated genre; main data not shipped

data_files_note: Only ancillary datasets for motivating figures are shipped; master_data.dta needed for Tables 2-7 is absent (proprietary Publishers Marketplace and Bowker).
priority_note: Not eligible: single-date genre DiD; main data not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (README.pdf, combine_data.do, table2-7 do-files). No article text available.
